items.title: Willie Hightower Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: And that band, I stayed with that band two years and seven months. Armand J.P. Rons band, until P. Rons got a job at the St. Charles Hotel.

ctx.x: He played with Ory and Mud Carey and some of that. Yeah, that's right.

He played with Ory and Mud Carey there. But he didn't depend on music too much because he was a decorator. He decorated. But he was a very independent little fellow. He bought a home there, see, in the Uptown, up by Protection Levy. And that band, I stayed with that band two years and seven months. Armand J.P. Rons band, until P. Rons got a job at the St. Charles Hotel. And he took four pieces, or five pieces over there, and turned this band over to me. But he didn't take no man out of this band. He used all…

items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Zoo was playing trombone in P. Ronce's band.

ctx.x: Then after I got in the district, as I told you, Zoo was playing trombone in P. Ronce's band. And most of the musicians from downtown, they didn't like Creoles, they didn't like nobody, stayed uptown, because I didn't speak French, see? And Manuel Perez, that's a trumpet player? Yes, that's right. That had the Exsulsa, that was the Exsulsa? Sometime the Enruid band. Enruid, Enruid band. And he had Joe playing trumpet with him. And he was playing cornet. And Sue Zoo was his trombone player. Zoo was one trombone…

Well, they still do, yes. They still do that. Every Sunday there'll be a parade in the summertime. Two weeks ago, before I came up, there were three parades that Sunday. Is that so? Yeah. And they still bury with the band? Yes. Not so many, but maybe one a week there'll be a few... There are lodges and things, good clubs.
